blocks.text: On 1 October 1960 the Union Jack came down in Lagos and the green-white-green went up. Nigeria's land, people and civil service were much the same the next morning. What changed was sovereignty — the final say now belonged to Nigerians.

blocks.markdown: **Sovereignty** is the supreme, final and absolute law-making power of a state within its own territory, and its freedom from external control. Whoever has the last word — the power no other body inside the state can overrule — holds sovereignty.

blocks.title: Sovereignty
blocks.text: The supreme legal authority of a state to make and enforce laws within its territory without being subject to any higher internal authority or to external dictation.

items: **Absoluteness** — no higher authority exists within the state to override it.
**Indivisibility** — sovereignty itself cannot be shared out, although its *exercise* can be distributed among organs and levels of government.
**Permanence** — it survives the fall of any particular government; it belongs to the state, not the ruler.
**Universality** — it covers every person and association within the territory.
**Inalienability** — the state cannot surrender it without ceasing to be a state.
**Exclusiveness** — only one sovereign authority may exist in a given territory.

blocks.markdown:
### Types of sovereignty

**Internal sovereignty** is supremacy over all persons, groups and institutions inside the state. **External sovereignty** is independence from the control of any other state.

**Legal sovereignty** belongs to the body legally empowered to make binding law — in Nigeria, the National Assembly acting within the Constitution. **Political sovereignty** belongs to the electorate, whose votes ultimately determine who wields legal power. **Popular sovereignty** is the doctrine that authority derives from the people, which is why the 1999 Constitution opens with the words "We the people of the Federal Republic of Nigeria".

**De jure** sovereignty is sovereignty recognised by law; **de facto** sovereignty is actual control on the ground. A military regime holds de facto power; a lawfully elected government holds de jure authority. In stable states the two coincide.

### Limitations on sovereignty in practice

In theory sovereignty is absolute; in practice every state is constrained by international law and treaty obligations, by membership of organisations such as the United Nations, the African Union and ECOWAS, by international public opinion, by economic dependence on trade, aid and loans, and by the constitution and courts of the state itself.

blocks.caption: State, nation and related concepts distinguished

blocks.title: State versus government
blocks.text: The state is permanent, abstract and sovereign; government is temporary, concrete and merely the agent of the state. Governments change every four years in Nigeria, but the Nigerian state continues — and it is the state, not the government of the day, that owes and is owed the country's debts and treaties.

blocks.title: Locating sovereignty in a constitutional dispute
blocks.prompt: A state governor argues that because his state government was elected by its own people, it may ignore a federal law on mineral resources. Where does sovereignty lie, and how should the dispute be resolved?

steps.text: Identify the level at which sovereignty resides. In a federation, sovereignty belongs to the state as a whole — the Federal Republic — and not to any constituent unit; the units exercise only powers the constitution allocates to them.

Check the constitutional allocation. Mines and minerals, including oil fields and natural gas, appear on the Exclusive Legislative List in the Second Schedule to the 1999 Constitution, so only the National Assembly may legislate on them.

Apply the supremacy rule. Where a valid federal law and a state position conflict on a matter within federal competence, the federal law prevails and the state position is void to the extent of the inconsistency.
Identify the proper forum. Disputes between the Federation and a state are decided by the Supreme Court, which has original jurisdiction over them.
Conclude: election by the people of one state confers a mandate to exercise state powers, not a share of sovereignty.

blocks.answer: Sovereignty lies with the Federal Republic as a whole; minerals are on the Exclusive Legislative List, so the federal law prevails and the Supreme Court would decide the dispute

blocks.title: The four elements of a state
blocks.text: Learn population, territory, government and sovereignty as a set, and remember that sovereignty is the element that separates a state from a mere society, a local council or a colony. Colonial Nigeria had the first three and lacked the fourth.

points: Sovereignty is the supreme, final law-making power of a state within its territory and its freedom from external control.
Its attributes are absoluteness, indivisibility, permanence, universality, inalienability and exclusiveness.
Sovereignty may be internal or external, legal or political, de jure or de facto.
In practice sovereignty is limited by international law, treaty obligations, economic dependence and the state's own constitution.
A state has population, territory, government and sovereignty; a nation is a people sharing identity, and Nigeria is a multi-national state.
